title: Units regulators and hR validation
objective: Audit and improve rigorous unit/regulator and zeta-residue performance, reuse exact splitting and interval work, and strengthen saturation/precision semantics with focused differential benchmarks

handoff.summary: Audited and optimized the ordinary strict-Python analytic proof layer after the integrated batched splitting work. RealBall arithmetic now rounds directly to dyadic endpoints without normalized-rational temporaries. An explicit field/provider-bound ZetaLogResidueWorkspace reuses authenticated splitting tails, exact aggregated prime-power plans, theorem thresholds, and certified finite-term intervals; the representative discriminant-5 cutoff reduces 1,534 raw contributions to 800 exact nonzero terms. Independent precision attempts are intersected, and regulator/zeta results record attempt counts and widths. Regulator providers must honor requested precision and give consistent refinements. Unit p-saturation evidence now records a doubling precision history, binds the decisive precision to the final attempt, and requires a genuine p-divisible enlargement index for nonmaximal results. Focused quadratic/cubic oracle checks, warm-cache isolation, precision escalation, hR index validation, and strict Pyright all pass.
risks: Rigorous zeta status assumes the caller supplies the actual maximal-order discriminant and a complete exact splitting provider; the function validates prime coverage and every local degree identity but does not independently prove the field/order identity.

Unit p-saturation remains a verification interface: only evidence whose certificate replay succeeds and whose doubling/decisive-precision metadata is internally consistent becomes rigorous. This lane does not implement the algebraic p-th-root obstruction producer, so an unchecked search remains explicitly unverified.

The common base had no public RealBall enclosure transport. This module therefore uses exact rational endpoints and mpmath.libmp directed-rounding intervals; future Arb transport can supply the same lower/upper protocol without changing proof states.

FactoredNumberFieldElement currently exposes only scalar qqbarLogAbsBall calls. The measured strict-Python regulator determinant is already sub-millisecond for the rank-two fixture, while zeta finite-interval evaluation dominated the profile, so this lane did not add an unmeasured algebraic-log batch boundary.

The lane worktree has no built FLINT addon, so generated Sage.js/native validation could not run locally. Per coordinator direction, this handoff stays active with focused receipts; central integration owns the broad native gate.
next_steps: Integration may retain a ZetaLogResidueWorkspace beside the analytic context when independent callers request the same field residue at several tolerances; the workspace rejects degree or provider identity changes.
Run pnpm test:native in central integration and move this contract to review only after recording that required receipt.
